name: Late Infantile Cerebellar Ataxia with Central Hypomyelination (CACH) Syndrome
aliases: Late Infantile Vanishing White Matter Disease
Late Infantile Leukodystrophy with Cerebellar Ataxia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Vanishing White Matter Disease Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Onset of progressive cerebellar ataxia and spasticity in late infancy or early childhood
MRI showing diffuse cerebral white matter rarefaction and cystic degeneration with vanishing white matter pattern
Identification of pathogenic biallelic mutations in EIF2B1-5 genes
Episodes of rapid neurological deterioration triggered by febrile illness or minor head trauma
Elevated cerebrospinal fluid glycine and lactate levels

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive cerebellar ataxia with characteristic MRI findings and confirmed pathogenic EIF2B mutations
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential for definitive diagnosis; clinical presentation and MRI findings guide initial suspicion.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Diffuse cerebral white matter rarefaction with cystic degeneration on MRI
searchTerms: brain white matter loss with cysts on MRI
cystic degeneration of brain white matter

pathognomonic.symptomName: Episodes of rapid neurological deterioration triggered by febrile illness
searchTerms: brain function decline triggered by illness

laboratory: Elevated cerebrospinal fluid glycine and lactate
imaging: MRI showing diffuse cerebral white matter rarefaction and cystic degeneration
Vanishing white matter pattern on T2-weighted MRI
other: Episodes of neurological deterioration triggered by stressors such as fever or minor trauma

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of Rosenthal fibers on biopsy
Frontal predominant white matter changes on MRI
Distinctive MRI pattern with tigroid appearance

redFlags: Rapid neurological deterioration following febrile illness
Progressive cerebellar ataxia in infancy or early childhood
Characteristic vanishing white matter pattern on MRI
references: van der Knaap MS, et al. Vanishing white matter disease: a review. J Child Neurol. 2006.
Bugiani M, et al. EIF2B-related disorders: clinical and genetic features. Brain. 2010.
Orphanet: Late infantile CACH syndrome. Orphanet Report Series, 2023.
